title: Access & Cost Governance Runbook Handover
topics: KMS/HSM rotation plan and runbook updates
Billing tag governance and cost allocation rules
RBAC/SSO access mapping for infra and admin roles
On-call and escalation handover for billing incidents
action_items: Priya - Publish v1.2 of Access & Cost Runbook to Confluence and notify stakeholders - due 2026-02-23
Ben - Share updated cost-tag mapping spreadsheet with product teams and set enforcement date (auto-tagging pilot) - due 2026-03-01
Marco - Produce short KMS rotation playbook (HSM steps + rollback) and attach to runbook - due 2026-02-25
Devon - Add on-call run escalation steps for billing alerts in PagerDuty and validate routes - due 2026-02-27
Aisha - Compile SOC2 artifacts list and confirm owners for each artifact - due 2026-03-03
next_steps: Agree final KMS window for 2026-03-10 (Priya/Marco to confirm by 2026-02-23)
Run two-week auto-tagging pilot for non-prod costs and report delta to FinOps (Ben)
Schedule cross-team dry-run of rotation playbook with SRE, Security, and FinOps - target week of 2026-03-02

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-18 09:30 PT | Duration: 1:02 | Zoom | Host: Priya Nair
Attendees: Priya Nair, Ben Lowe, Marco Reyes, Leah Chen, James Holt, Sara Kim, Devon Park, Aisha Patel
Summary: Quick handover meeting to finalize the Access & Cost Governance runbook, confirm KMS rotation playbook, align tagging enforcement and on-call escalation for billing. A few clarifications on SOC2 artifact owners and a dry-run for KMS rotation.

[00:00] Priya: Okay folks, thanks for squeezing this in, I know this morning is busy. The goal today is to hand over the runbook edits from IT side, confirm the KMS rotation window and make sure FinOps tagging rules are aligned with the cost dashboards, and that security has a clear playbook.
[00:18] Ben: Yep, I can hear you. Mostly I want to be sure the cost allocation bits are explicit — like, what tags we auto-enforce, which ones are advisory, and who owns the mapping spreadsheet. Last quarter we had a few untagged clusters and it made the chargeback murky.
[00:32] Marco: Also want to flag that the KMS rotation steps need HSM steps called out for the private deployments; last time the doc had the generic KMS wording and folks got confused about the hardware steps.
[00:45] Priya: Totally. Leah, I sent the draft link earlier — Confluence: /internal/runbooks/access-cost-governance (note: internal link). The doc has sections: roles, KMS rotation, tagging, on-call, and SOC2 artifacts. This meeting is to accept final edits.
[01:05] Leah: I added a short matrix mapping RBAC roles to the Confluence groups; it's rough but should help SRE and Product Ops agree on who can trigger rotations or change tags.
[01:20] Devon: Quick interruption — on the PagerDuty routing, do we have an explicit billing alert policy? I recall there being two severities: P1 for cost spikes that indicate potential runaway, and P2 for reporting anomalies.
[01:34] Ben: Right, P1 is runaway spend — auto scale gone wrong, misconfiguration — that needs on-call SRE + FinOps. P2 is basically accounting mismatches. We should put the routing in the runbook.
[01:47] Marco: On the KMS schedule: suggested rotation window is a 2-hour maintenance window during low traffic, ideally 03:00 UTC. We need backups and a rollback plan. Also, clarify whether rotation is key version bump vs re-encrypt. The vendor docs use different terms and the transcript might call it a rekey, which confuses people.
[02:10] Priya: Good call. I'll change wording to 'key rotation (version-increment + re-encrypt step optional)' and add a vendor appendix.
[02:25] Sara: From billing side, auto-tagging needs to be opt-out for dev workloads, opt-in for prod, but enforcement should start for non-prod to get the data quality. Ben, you mentioned auto-tagging pilot?
[02:40] Ben: Yes, pilot on non-prod EC2/GPU pools and storage buckets. We'll run for two weeks and compare the accuracy of the mapping. If >95% accuracy, enable enforcement in non-prod. We'll then look at staged enforcement in prod.
[02:56] James: Are there cost allocation implications with Dedicated clusters? We need to ensure reserved capacity is attributed properly when shared across teams. The runbook should recommend labeling patterns for dedicated vs shared pools.
[03:12] Leah: I put examples in the runbook: team:<team>, env:<prod|stage|dev>, pool:<dedicated|shared>, billing_unit:<product-family>. Should we standardize on those?
[03:28] Devon: Works for SRE, as long as we include a regex or tag validation rule in Terraform modules.
[03:40] Priya: I'll add a snippet for TF modules so tags are enforced at provisioning. Note: transcription may say 'Terraforms' sometimes — we should be consistent.
[03:52] Marco: Back to KMS/HSM: for private on-prem deployments, the HSM rotation requires a manual step with the appliance console. I recommend we include a checklist: pre-rotation snapshot, test rotation in staging hardware, notify customers with private deployments, then rotate in prod. Also add contact for the HSM vendor support.
[04:15] Ben: Good. Also we should confirm whether rotation affects token signing keys vs data-encryption keys. Those are separate buckets. The runbook should mask which services rely on which KMS key IDs.
[04:33] Aisha: For SOC2, we need artifact owners. I can take compliance owner for the rotation evidence and logs retention proof. But who will own the billing artifact for cost allocation reconciliation?
[04:45] Sara: Billing team will own cost reconciliation artifacts; I'll own the ledger and the reconciled spreadsheet.
[04:53] Priya: OK, assign: Aisha - rotation evidence and retention; Sara - cost reconciliation artifacts. I'll put those names in the runbook.
[05:02] (short crosstalk)
[05:10] Leah: One small nit: the document currently references 'KV cache' in a couple places which is irrelevant to this runbook — that was copy-pasted from a runtime doc. I'll remove the runtime-specific bits since they confuse the auditors.
[05:24] Marco: Yeah I've seen that, it's better to keep this runbook focused.
[05:30] Ben: On the enforcement timeline: we suggested enforcement for non-prod starting 2026-03-15 to give teams time to fix tags. Is that still acceptable?
[05:42] James: Timeline OK for infra, but product teams need a heads-up. Suggest a communication plan: announcement + two office hours sessions.
[05:52] Leah: I'll schedule two office hours and record them. One focused on tagging, second on rotation/playbook walkthrough.
[06:02] Priya: Great. Marco, can you run a dry-run of the rotation playbook with Devon and maybe Sara to test impact on billing flows?
[06:12] Marco: Yes. I'll set up a dry-run in staging with the HSM appliance next week. Devon, please coordinate with me on test workloads.
[06:20] Devon: Yep, will do.
[06:24] Ben: A note on dashboards — we should tag the cost dashboards with the enforcement status so finance can filter. I'll add a 'tagging_enforced' flag in the dashboard metadata.
[06:36] Sara: Helpful. Also, can we add an alert when a new untagged resource appears above $500/month? That could be a threshold for an investigation.
[06:46] Priya: We'll add that to the runbook's monitoring section. Devon, can SRE add a Prometheus exporter or cheap lambda to scan tags and push to PagerDuty?
[07:00] Devon: I can add a lambda that runs daily and fires an alert to PagerDuty. Low overhead.
[07:08] (brief typing/noise)
[07:20] Marco: Small transcription glitch note — sometimes speaker IDs get swapped in Fireflies, e.g., it writes 'Speaker 2' for me. Ignore that in minutes.
[07:30] Priya: Thanks. Any other concerns?
[07:35] Aisha: One more compliance ask — we need to keep rotation logs for 1 year and provide a signed attestation for SOC2 review. Make sure the runbook includes retention policy and who signs.
[07:48] Marco: We'll store rotation events in the central audit index (syslog -> secure bucket), and Aisha will have access. I'll add the exact retention command to the appendix.
[08:00] Ben: Finance also wants an exported monthly CSV of tag coverage for auditors. I can automate that once tagging enforcement lands.
[08:10] Leah: I'm going to add a 'change freeze' step for rotation windows in the runbook — any deploys blocked for that 2-hour window. Add exception process if emergency deploy required.
[08:22] Priya: Good. Let's recap the decisions and owners.
[08:28] (Recap) Priya: KMS rotation target 2026-03-10, 03:00 UTC maintenance window, Marco to draft HSM playbook and run staging dry-run, Devon to coordinate tests, Ben to run two-week non-prod auto-tagging pilot starting ~2026-02-24, Leah to schedule two office hours and publish runbook v1.2 on Confluence, Aisha to own SOC2 artifacts for rotation, Sara to own cost reconciliation artifacts.
[09:00] James: And we agreed to runbook v1.2 updates by 2026-02-23, after which we send the invite for the walkthrough.
[09:12] Priya: Perfect. Any final questions?
[09:16] (silence)
[09:18] Priya: If not, we'll close. I'll post the updated doc and ping the channel. Thanks all.

End of meeting notes.

References: runbook draft link (internal): https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Access+%26+Cost+Governance (internal), cost-tag-mapping spreadsheet (internal): /sheets/finops/cost_tag_mapping_v2.xlsx, HSM vendor support contact: hsm-support@vendor.example (placeholder).

Notes on transcription: There are occasional mis-hearings ("Terraforms" vs Terraform, "rekey" vs rotation, speaker labels inconsistent). The timestamps are approximate (Fireflies exported every ~30s).
